building.name: International Building Code, as adopted and amended by Kansas City Code of Ordinances Chapter 18 (Building and Rehabilitation Code), Article II, Section 18-40
building.local_amendments_note: Section 18-40 deletes Chapter 1 (administration is Article I of Chapter 18) and amends, among others, 1004.9 (posting of occupant load), 1109.2.1.8 (universal changing station, added by Ordinance 210181), 1110.4.13.1 (school play areas, Ordinance 220353) and Table 2902.1 (footnote g, drinking fountains only). No amendment to Chapter 8 (interior finishes, so 803.9 on HDPE stands), to Table 1004.5 (floor area per occupant) or to the toilet and urinal ratios of Table 2902.1 or Sections 2902.1.1, 2902.1.2 and 2902.2.
building.effective_note: Committee Substitute for Ordinance 200418 passed the Council on 2020-06-18 (Legistar history); Legistar shows 2020-06-28 as its date in force, and a search extract of the city's Building and Rehabilitation Code page gives the same effective date (the page itself returns 403). Section 18-40 was last re-enacted by Committee Substitute for Ordinance 220353, passed 2022-05-19.
building.quote: Sec. 18-40. Adoption of International Building Code (2018); amendments. The International Building Code (2018), promulgated by the International Code Council, is adopted and incorporated in this article by reference as if fully set forth, except as it is amended by the following provisions of this section.

plumbing.name: Uniform Plumbing Code, as adopted and amended by Kansas City Code of Ordinances Chapter 18, Article VII, Section 18-125
plumbing.local_amendments_note: Section 18-125 deletes the plumbing code's own fixture-count rules (422.1 through 422.4 and Table 422.1) and sends the reader to Article II, the building code. The number of toilets in Kansas City therefore comes from the 2018 International Building Code, Chapter 29, not from the Uniform Plumbing Code.
plumbing.quote: Sec. 18-125. Adoption of Uniform Plumbing Code (2018); amendments. The Uniform Plumbing Code (2018), promulgated by the International Association of Plumbing and Mechanical Officials, is adopted and incorporated in this article by reference as if fully set forth, except as it is amended by the following provisions of this section. [...] 422.0 Minimum Number of Required Fixtures. See Article II of this chapter. 422.1 through 422.4 and Table 422.1 are deleted.

also_adopted: International Energy Conservation Code (2021), Section 18-367 (Ordinance 220364, amended by Ordinance 260144 in February 2026)
codes.scheduled_change_note: No dated change. Ordinance 260137 (passed 2026-02-05) directs the City Manager to develop recommendations for adopting the 2024 International Code series. No ordinance adopting the 2024 codes appears in the City Clerk's Legistar records up to 2026-11-24 (title searches for 'Chapter 18', 'International Building Code', 'model codes', '2024 International'). The city's SpeakEasy project page 'Updating Kansas City's building codes' exists but shows no text without JavaScript.

fixtures.basis: Kansas City takes its toilet counts from the 2018 International Building Code, Table 2902.1, which is the same table the Missouri state pack used as the model. The city's only change to the table is footnote g on drinking fountains. The split in half (2902.1.1), rounding up, the small-occupancy exceptions (2902.2) and the ratios for offices, restaurants and schools are unamended, so the state pack's worked examples stand as Kansas City's own. One open point: the table sends the reader to Section 424.2 of the International Plumbing Code for urinals, and Section 18-40 says a reference to a plumbing code means the code the city adopted, the Uniform Plumbing Code, whose own fixture rules (422.1 to 422.4, Table 422.1) the city deleted. The adopted text therefore states no limit on how many men's toilets may be urinals.
fixtures.quote: Table 2902.1 Minimum Number of Required Plumbing Fixtures - Add footnote g to column "DRINKING FOUNTAINS" as follows: g. Where restaurants or other businesses serving take-out food or drinks provide drinking water in a container free of charge, drinking fountains shall not be required in those restaurants or those other businesses serving take-out food or drinks. In other occupancies where drinking fountains are required, water coolers or bottled water dispensers shall be permitted to be substituted for not more than 50 percent of the required number of drinking fountains.
fixtures.reference_quote: All references within the model codes to any building, electrical, gas, mechanical, plumbing, sewage disposal, elevator, energy conservation, or existing building code shall be construed to be a reference to the respective building, electrical, gas, mechanical, plumbing, sewage disposal, elevator, energy conservation, or existing building code specifically adopted by reference in Articles II through XIV of this chapter.
fixtures.table_header_quote: WATER CLOSETS (URINALS SEE SECTION 424.2 OF THE INTERNATIONAL PLUMBING CODE)
fixtures.hdpe_fire: Applies. Kansas City adopted the 2018 International Building Code with no amendment to Chapter 8, so Section 803.9 (HDPE and polypropylene interior finish must meet the NFPA 286 room test, quoted in the state pack) is in force.
fixtures.occupant_load: Unamended Table 1004.5 of the 2018 International Building Code: business areas 150 gross, assembly with tables and chairs 15 net, classroom 20 net (quoted in the state pack). The city's only change in Section 1004 is 1004.9, posting of the occupant load.
fixtures.confidence_note: The city's amendments were read in the Clerk's official ordinance text. The model table and sections were read on UpCodes (secondary copy). The urinal limit is open.

permit.exempt_list_quote: Sec. 18-16(b) Exempted work. A permit shall not be required for the types of work in each of the separate classes of permit as listed in this subsection. Exemption from the permit requirements of this code shall not be deemed to grant authorization for any work to be done in violation of the provisions of this code or any other laws or ordinances of the city. (1) Building permits. A building permit shall not be required for the following: a. One-story detached accessory buildings used as tool and storage sheds, playhouses, garages, carports, and similar uses, provided the projected roof area does not exceed 200 square feet (18.58 m2). b. Oil derricks. c. Movable cases, counters and partitions not over five feet nine inches (1753 mm) in height. d. Retaining walls which are not over 4 feet (1219 mm) in height [...] e. Fences. [...] n. Replacement of doors and windows in existing openings where fire resistance, smoke control and opening protection are not required by Article II. o. Repairs of holes in plaster or gypsum board walls. p. Installation or replacement of wall or floor mounted cabinets (kitchen, bath, etc.). q. Painting, papering, installation of carpeting/floor coverings and similar finish work. r. Installation or replacement of exterior gutters and downspouts. s. Tuckpointing brick and/or stone masonry. [...] u. Replacement of interior or exterior trimwork. v. Boarding up vacant buildings. [...]
permit.note: Toilet partitions or compartments are not named. Item c exempts 'Movable cases, counters and partitions not over five feet nine inches', the model code's wording for movable office-type partitions; whether the city reads a floor-anchored or ceiling-hung toilet partition as 'movable', and how it measures height, is not stated. Section 18-16(a)(1) requires a permit to 'construct, enlarge, alter' a structure, and Section 18-4(b) lets 'ordinary repairs' go without application or notice but excludes 'the cutting away of any wall, partition or portion thereof'. The text is Section 18-16 as enacted by Committee Substitute for Ordinance 200418 (2020); no later ordinance naming Section 18-16 was found in Legistar, but the codified section on Municode and the city's 'Building Permit Exempt Work' page (kcmo.gov, 403) were not opened.
permit.general_rule_quote: It shall be unlawful to construct, enlarge, alter, move, raise, shore, demolish, wreck or raze a structure or parking station; [...] unless a separate permit for each building, premise or structure has first been obtained; provided, however, that repairs, as defined in section 18-4(b), which do not involve any violation of this code, and work as specified in subsection (b) of this section, shall be exempted from this provision.
permit.repairs_quote: (b) Ordinary repairs. Application or notice to the building official is not required for ordinary repairs to structures, replacement of lamps or the connection of approved portable electrical equipment to approved permanently installed receptacles. Such repairs shall not include the cutting away of any wall, partition or portion thereof, the removal or cutting of any structural beam or load bearing support, or the removal or change of any required means of egress [...]
permit.office: City Planning & Development Department, Permits Division, City Hall, 414 E. 12th St., 5th Floor, Kansas City, MO 64106

restrooms_city.rule: Kansas City adds one rule to the 2018 model code: a family or assisted-use toilet room must include a universal (adult-size, height-adjustable) changing station; where a building has more than one such room, one is enough if signs at the others point to it. The city does not amend the model code's sign rule (single-user and family rooms 'identified for use by either sex') or its rule that separate facilities are provided for each sex above the small-occupancy limits; the 2018 text has no exception for a shared multi-stall all-gender room. No separate city ordinance on restroom signs was found: Resolution 210461 (2021), on all-gender restrooms in city-owned property, shows no passage in Legistar.
restrooms_city.quote: 1109.2.1.8 Universal Changing Station. Family or assisted-use toilet and bathing rooms shall include a universal changing station for the assistance of persons with disabilities. The changing station area must be equipped with a height-adjustable changing table suitable for use for an adult or a child. The table shall be: a) of minimum dimension 24 inches in width by 70 inches in length; b) adjustable to allow lowering to a height no greater than 8 inches, and raising to a height no less than 34", above finished floor elevation; and, c) capable of supporting a minimum of 350 pounds. Exception: Where a building is provided with more than one family or assisted-use toilet and bathing room, only one such room shall require a Universal Changing Station. Where this exception is utilized, signage shall be provided at all such rooms indicating the location of the Universal Changing Station.

model_quotes.single_user_sign: Single-user toilet facilities and bathing rooms, and family or assisted-use toilet rooms and bathing rooms shall be identified for use by either sex. (2018 IBC 2902.1.2)
model_quotes.separate_facilities: Where plumbing fixtures are required, separate facilities shall be provided for each sex. Exceptions: [...] total occupant load, including both employees and customers, of 15 or fewer [...] mercantile occupancies in which the maximum occupant load is 100 or fewer [...] business occupancies in which the maximum occupant load is 25 or fewer. (2018 IBC 2902.2)
model_quotes.family_room_required: In assembly and mercantile occupancies, an accessible family or assisted-use toilet room shall be provided where an aggregate of six or more male and female water closets is required. (2018 IBC 1109.2.1)

page.meta: Commercial bathroom partitions delivered to Kansas City job sites. Price your restroom, pick a material and see the city rules and tax that apply.
page.lead: Commercial bathroom partitions for Kansas City offices, schools, distribution centers and sports venues, shipped by freight to your job site.
page.fire_bullet: - **Fire safety:** Kansas City's building rules require solid plastic (HDPE) partitions to pass a room fire test. Ask for the fire-rated version.
page.stall_bullet: - **How many stalls:** Kansas City sets the number of toilets by how many people use the building. The table below shows what that means.
page.restroom_bullet: - **Single-user and all-gender restrooms:** Missouri has no state law on single-user or all-gender restrooms, and none on who may use which restroom. Under Kansas City's building rules a one-person or family restroom is marked for use by either sex. Above the small-building limits the rules call for separate men's and women's rooms, and they have no provision for a shared all-gender room with stalls. A family restroom, which larger stores and gathering places must have, needs an adult-size changing table that adjusts in height.
page.permit_bullet: - **Permits:** Kansas City's list of work that needs no building permit includes movable cases, counters and partitions up to 5 feet 9 inches high, wall or floor mounted cabinets, and painting and similar finish work. It doesn't name toilet partitions. Ask the City Planning and Development Department's Permits Division at (816) 513-1500 whether your replacement needs one. You don't need a permit to buy partitions.
page.confirm_office: Kansas City's City Planning and Development Department
page.stalls_intro: Kansas City counts toilets by a building's capacity: the most people it is designed to hold at one time, worked out from its floor area. It isn't the number of staff or of visitors in a day. Half are counted as men and half as women. Every toilet needs a stall, and each urinal needs a screen. Urinals may take the place of some of the men's toilets. The model rules cap that at half in an office and two thirds in a restaurant or school, but the cap sits in a plumbing code Kansas City hasn't adopted, so confirm the share with the City Planning and Development Department.
page.stalls_after: These are minimums for the whole building. Separate men's and women's rooms aren't required in a space for 15 people or fewer, in an office for 25 or fewer or in a store for 100 or fewer. At least one stall in each room must be wheelchair accessible.
page.capacity: To find your building's capacity, Kansas City's building rules count an office at one person per 150 square feet of floor, a restaurant dining room at one per 15 square feet and a classroom at one per 20. Your architect or the City Planning and Development Department sets the final number.
page.install_rule: Kansas City licenses specific trades and residential builders before they pull permits; confirm with City Planning and Development what applies to partition installation. Missouri has no state license for general or specialty interior contractors such as partition installers. You don't need a permit to buy partitions.
page.faq_install_extra: Missouri has no state license for partition installers, and Kansas City licenses specific trades and residential builders.
page.public_jobs_bullet: - **Public jobs:** on state, city, county and school district projects with a total cost above $75,000, Missouri law requires at least the wage the state sets each year for each trade in each county. For a carpenter on building work in Jackson County that is $68.84 an hour, benefits included.
page.sales_tax_bullet: - **Sales tax:** 8.975% at most Kansas City addresses in Jackson County: 4.225% state, 1.5% county and zoo district and 3.25% city. Addresses inside the Main Street rail district pay 9.975%, and some shopping districts add their own tax. Partitions shipped in from a seller outside Missouri fall under the use tax instead, 7.475% at those addresses. The parts of the city in Clay, Platte and Cass counties have their own rates.
page.buyers_extra: - **Stadiums, arenas and convention halls:** HDPE or phenolic stalls that stand up to event crowds and nightly washdown.
sources: - Codes Kansas City enforces: Kansas City Code of Ordinances, Chapter 18 (Building and Rehabilitation Code), as enacted by [Committee Substitute for Ordinance 200418](https://kansascity.legistar1.com/kansascity/attachments/760b1de0-80c6-477f-a866-95b066acb5dc.docx) (passed June 18, 2020, in force June 28, 2020; [signed copy](https://kansascity.legistar1.com/kansascity/attachments/a23c7773-3ccf-4267-bf1d-1ffd4e509b0a.pdf)): Section 18-40, International Building Code (2018) with amendments, last re-enacted by [Committee Substitute for Ordinance 220353](https://webapi.legistar.com/v1/kansascity/matters/42517/texts/5219) (passed May 19, 2022), and Section 18-125, Uniform Plumbing Code (2018) with amendments. Read in the [City Clerk's legislation records](https://clerk.kcmo.gov/Legislation.aspx). Checked 2026-11-24.

- Toilet counts in Kansas City: Section 18-125 deletes Sections 422.1 to 422.4 and Table 422.1 of the Uniform Plumbing Code and refers to the building code; Section 18-40 changes Table 2902.1 of the 2018 International Building Code only by a footnote on drinking fountains ([Ordinance 220353](https://webapi.legistar.com/v1/kansascity/matters/42517/texts/5219)). The table and Sections 2902.1.1, 2902.1.2 and 2902.2 were read on a secondary copy ([UpCodes](https://up.codes/viewer/missouri/ibc-2018/chapter/29/plumbing-systems)). The table refers to Section 424.2 of the International Plumbing Code for urinals, a code Kansas City has not adopted. Checked 2026-11-24.

- Family restrooms and the adult changing table: Section 18-40, added Section 1109.2.1.8 ([Ordinance 220353](https://webapi.legistar.com/v1/kansascity/matters/42517/texts/5219), first added by Ordinance 210181 in 2021); 2018 International Building Code, Section 1109.2.1, read on [UpCodes](https://up.codes/viewer/missouri/ibc-2018/chapter/11/accessibility). Checked 2026-11-24.

- Work exempt from a building permit in Kansas City: Code of Ordinances, Sections 18-16(a)(1), 18-16(b)(1) and 18-4(b), as enacted by [Ordinance 200418](https://kansascity.legistar1.com/kansascity/attachments/760b1de0-80c6-477f-a866-95b066acb5dc.docx). Checked 2026-11-24.

- Licensed trades and the Permits Division's phone number: Code of Ordinances, Section 18-14 ([Ordinance 200418](https://kansascity.legistar1.com/kansascity/attachments/760b1de0-80c6-477f-a866-95b066acb5dc.docx)); [KC BizCare, Contractor Licensing](https://bizcare.kcmo.gov/contractor-licensing). Checked 2026-11-24.

- Sales and use tax in Kansas City: [Missouri Department of Revenue, Sales and Use Tax Rate Tables, October to December 2026](https://dor.mo.gov/pdf/rates/2026/october2026.pdf), jurisdictions 38000-095-000 (Kansas City, Jackson County), 38000-095-009 (with the Kansas City Main Street Rail TDD) and 00000-095-000 (Jackson County). Checked 2026-11-24.

- Jackson County carpenter rate on public building work: [Missouri Division of Labor Standards, Annual Wage Order No. 33, Section 048, Jackson County](https://laborwebapps.mo.gov/DLS/PrevailingWage/AWO/33/33_WO048.pdf), in effect since May 29, 2026 per the [Annual Wage Order look-up](https://laborwebapps.mo.gov/dls/prevailingwage). Checked 2026-11-24.
page.official_names: - The rules by their official names: 2010 ADA Standards for Accessible Design; Kansas City Code of Ordinances, Chapter 18, Building and Rehabilitation Code: International Building Code (2018) with local amendments (Section 18-40) and Uniform Plumbing Code (2018) with local amendments (Section 18-125), in force since June 28, 2020; ICC A117.1-2009 as referenced by the 2018 International Building Code, and the most recent ANSI A117.1 for publicly funded buildings under RSMo 8.610 to 8.655; Section 18-16 for work exempt from permits; NFPA 286 for HDPE under Section 803.9 of the International Building Code; Missouri Prevailing Wage Law, RSMo 290.210 to 290.340, Annual Wage Order No. 33.
notes: To confirm by phone before launch: whether replacing or adding floor-anchored toilet partitions in an existing commercial restroom needs a Kansas City building permit (Permits Division, (816) 513-1500); the exempt list names only movable partitions up to 5 feet 9 inches.

To confirm by phone: how many men's toilets may be urinals in Kansas City. The city's toilet table points to a section of the International Plumbing Code, but the city adopted the Uniform Plumbing Code and deleted that code's fixture rules.

Chapter 18 was read in the City Clerk's ordinance files (Ordinances 200418 and 220353), not in the codified code: Municode and every kcmo.gov page blocked automated reading. Open Chapter 18 on Municode in a browser once and compare Sections 18-16, 18-40 and 18-125.

Kansas City is preparing a move to the 2024 codes: Ordinance 260137 (February 5, 2026) tells the City Manager to develop recommendations. No adoption ordinance was on file on 2026-11-24. Recheck before launch and rebuild the stall table when one passes (the 2024 model rules change the single-user sign wording and allow shared all-gender rooms).

Sales tax: confirm on the Department of Revenue's address lookup that the delivery address is inside or outside the Main Street Rail district; the split of the 1.5% between Jackson County and the zoo district was worked out by difference, not read. Read the January 2027 rate table when it is posted.
Confirm with Abe's accountant that Next Partitions' shipments into Kansas City are charged the 7.475% use tax, not the 8.975% sales tax.

The wage order's building-rates page was read from the page image (its text layer is garbled): $68.84 for Carpenter, Jackson County. The parts of Kansas City in Clay, Platte and Cass counties have their own wage orders.
The Missouri state pack's fire-safety, stall and capacity wording describes model rules; this page replaces it with Kansas City's own code, which is the 2018 edition those model rules come from.
